text:
anya: quick heads-up — seeing a perf regression when serving Flash/fused/paged attention across SM80 vs SM90 machines after the CUDA 12.4 upgrade. numbers below, need to sync on root cause and short-term fallback.

matt: any reproducer? batch/seq distribution?

anya: small repro attached in thread (local), seq=2048, batch=8. baseline on SM80 + CUDA 12.2: ~420 tok/s; on SM90 + CUDA 12.4: ~300 tok/s using our Triton kernels.

matt: ran a quick matrix this morning:
```
# config
model: 13B
seq: [512, 1024, 2048]
batch: [1,4,8]
kernels: [cuda-fused, triton-flash, paged-attn]
```
results (tokens/s, larger is better):
- SM80 CUDA12.2 triton-flash: 410
- SM80 CUDA12.2 cuda-fused: 430
- SM90 CUDA12.4 triton-flash: 295
- SM90 CUDA12.4 cuda-fused: 420
- SM90 CUDA12.4 paged-attn: 310

matt: interestingly the CUDA fused path on SM90 is fine, the Triton flash path regresses. suggests a Triton dispatch/kern else issue.

sai: log dump from runtime kernel selector when seq=2048, batch=8: 
```
[selector] candidates: [triton_flash_v2, cuda_fused_v1, paged_v3]
[selector] estimated_costs: [0.72, 0.65, 0.83]
[selector] chosen: triton_flash_v2
[sel-debug] sm_arch=90 cuda_version=12.4 cublaslt=enabled
[sel-debug] fallback_compat_check: true -> triggering opt path A
```
sai: note the selector's cost model shifted weights after the CUDA version change — the estimator now prefers triton_flash for long sequences even though empirically it's slower on SM90.

katie: we changed the continuous-batching heuristic last sprint (PR #3410) — thresholds for seq boundary aggregation grew from 1.2x->1.5x. could increase seq variance and push more requests into the long-seq path, exposing the regression.

josh: I bisected quickly — regression correlates with a Triton kernel update in PR #3427 (kernel rewrite for mem-coalesce). The new kernel uses a different shared memory pattern that seems to interact poorly with SM90 scheduler under CUDA12.4.

anya: can we get perf traces (nsight/cupti) for both good vs bad runs? need to check stall reasons: membound vs schd.

matt: attached a tiny nvprof summary (excerpt):
```
SM90+triton_flash: 72% memory_stall, 18% warp_issue, 10% compute
SM80+triton_flash: 28% memory_stall, 60% compute, 12% warp_issue
```
matt: big jump in memory stalls on SM90 triton path.

sai: KV cache note — on long sequences we hit more KV buffer churn; the Triton kernel variant reads/writes a compacted KV layout that triggers extra device->host syncs in our misc util on SM90 driver combo. probable cause for mem stalls.

katie: short-term mitigation options: 1) force cuda-fused path for SM90 + seq>1024 (config override), 2) revert PR #3427 in canary, 3) tune selector weights to prefer cuda-fused when mem_stall metric > X.

josh: I pushed a quick selector patch (`sel-hotfix`) that biases cost model +15% for triton_flash on arch>=90 until we root cause. will open a canary rollout.

infra-bot: CI perf job results for canary (sel-hotfix):
- canary group (10% traffic, SM90+Cuda12.4): p50 latency +2ms, p99 - unchanged, tok/s +28% vs baseline triton_flash
- no failures in SLO regression check

anya: good. long-term: we should add microbenchmarks that exercise the memory access pattern differences between the Triton and CUDA fused kernels across driver versions (12.2/12.4/12.5). also add a KV cache stress test to our e2e perf suite.

matt: agreed. I'll create a minimal repro harness that runs kernels with cupti counters and reproduces mem_stall pattern. will share link.

sai: i'll do a deeper code review of PR #3427 tomorrow and try a tweak in the shared-mem banking/sync (possible race/over-subscription pattern).

katie: for rollout plan: continue sel-hotfix canary for 24h, if stable promote, concurrently run bisect and microbench.

anya: thanks all — action items: matt: repro + cupti, sai: kernel review, josh: keep canary, katie: update rollout doc. I'll consolidate notes in a short postmortem if we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:
